title: Concavity cuts for the linear maxmin problem
contribution: Method to compute valid concavity cuts for the linear maxmin problem through a primal and a dual concave-programming reformulation (abstract).
problem_entry: Cutting planes for the linear maxmin problem. The entry is to obtain valid concavity cuts for maxmin, which needs the problem in concave-programming form (abstract).
key_idea: The problem is reformulated as a concave program with linear constraints in two ways, a primal and a dual approach, and valid concavity cuts are computed from each (abstract).

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: reformulation as a lens (transfer tests, not just solutions)
method_links.note: A concave-programming tool (concavity cuts) is carried over to maxmin through two reformulations, primal and dual.

quotes.text: We consider a primal and a dual approach.

title: Links between linear bilevel and mixed 0–1 programming problems
contribution: Big-constant-free reformulation of mixed 0-1 programs as linear bilevel programs, proof that MIP branch-and-bound is embedded in a bilevel branch-and-bound (identical subproblem sequences), and a new BLP optimality test with nonstandard penalties (abstract).
problem_entry: Links between linear bilevel programming (BLP) and linear mixed 0-1 programming. The new reformulation is presented as one that needs no large finite constant, which implies that earlier ones did (abstract).
key_idea: A new MIP0-1 → BLP reformulation with no large constant. Proof that classical MIP branch-and-bound is embedded in a bilevel branch-and-bound: on any instance and its reformulation both produce the same sequence of subproblems (abstract).

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: reformulation as a lens (transfer tests, not just solutions)
method_links.note: The reformulation is used to compare algorithms and to port a test (penalties) from MIP to BLP, not only to move solutions.

transferable: To compare two algorithms that live in different problem classes, prove that through the reformulation they generate identical subproblem sequences. Then port the stronger class's tests (here, penalties) to the other class (abstract).
coauthors: P. Hansen, B. Jaumard, G. Savard

quotes.text: A new reformulation of the linear mixed 0-1 programming problem into a bilevel linear programming one, which does not require the introduction of a large finite constant, is presented.
Moreover, we deduce a new optimality test for bilevel linear programming which makes use of nonstandard penalties.

contribution: Finite branch-and-bound enumeration of all Nash equilibria for strategic-form and sequence-form bimatrix games from complementary slackness of two pairs of parameterized LPs, with computational experience (abstract).
problem_entry: Enumerate all Nash equilibria, in finite time, of two-person games given in strategic form and in sequence form (abstract).
key_idea: Branch and bound on the complementary slackness conditions of two pairs of parameterized linear programs, with one algorithm for each form (abstract).

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: reformulation as a lens (transfer tests, not just solutions)
method_links.note: Equilibrium conditions are handled as complementary slackness of parameterized LPs. That this reuses the thesis maxmin/bilinear branching is taken from card b2-01 (ch. 4), not from this abstract.

coauthors: P. Hansen, B. Jaumard, G. Savard (GERAD page; works.json lists only "C Audet, ...")

quotes.text: For each forms, the algorithm exploits complementary slackness optimality conditions of two pairs of parameterized linear programming problems.

title: On the linear maxmin and related programming problems
contribution: Chapter linking linear maxmin, bilevel, disjoint bilinear and mixed 0-1 programming. It presents the Beale-Small-in-HJS embedding, concavity cuts for both symmetric maxmin reformulations, a finite branch and bound, numerical results and a bimatrix-game application (abstract).
problem_entry: The linear maxmin problem is a game played in sequence by two players with opposite objectives, in which the first player anticipates the opponent's reaction. It can be read as a special linear bilevel program or as a reformulation of disjoint bilinear programming (abstract).
key_idea: A map of links: MIP0-1 and BLP reformulate into each other, and Beale–Small's MIP algorithm is embedded in Hansen–Jaumard–Savard's BLP algorithm. Each maxmin problem has a symmetric partner through the bilinear reformulation, both give concavity cuts, and a branch and bound that exploits both is finite (abstract).

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: reformulation as a lens (transfer tests, not just solutions)
method_links.note: The whole chapter is organised as reformulation links, each one used to transfer algorithms, cuts or embeddings.

coauthors: P. Hansen, B. Jaumard, G. Savard

quotes.text: Moreover, the similarity between these problems is deeper.
We show how to exploit these symmetrical maxmin reformulations in order to obtain a finitely convergent branch and bound algorithm.

title: A symmetrical linear maxmin approach to disjoint bilinear programming
contribution: Two symmetric linear maxmin reformulations of disjoint bilinear programming, with a bijection of optima and no extra local optima. Their complementarity and monotonicity conditions give a finite exact branch and bound, and boundedness is shown to be strongly NP-complete (abstract).
problem_entry: Disjoint bilinear programming (BILD), and the question of whether its optimal value is bounded (abstract).
key_idea: BILD is reformulated as two distinct linear maxmin problems. There is a simple bijection between their optimal solutions and those of BILD, and they have no more local optima than BILD. The necessary optimality conditions of both reformulations (complementarity and monotonicity) drive a finite, exact branch and bound (abstract).

method_links.method: new-pattern candidate: reformulation as a lens (transfer tests, not just solutions)
method_links.note: Both symmetric reformulations are used at once, and their optimality conditions become the branching rules.

transferable: When you propose a reformulation, prove (i) a bijection between its optimal solutions and the original's and (ii) that it has no more local optima. "The reformulation adds no complexity" then becomes a theorem instead of a claim (abstract).
coauthors: P. Hansen, B. Jaumard, G. Savard

quotes.text: In that sense, the reformulations do not introduce additional complexity.
Determining if the optimal value of a bilinear programming problem is bounded is shown to be strongly NP-complete.

title: A surrogate-model-based method for constrained optimization
contribution: Surrogate-model-based constrained optimization method that pairs global exploration through response models with a provably convergent local mechanism, and addresses surrogate conditioning as points cluster (abstract).
problem_entry: Constrained optimization in which the objective and the constraints are represented by global surrogates (response models) of the true responses. Global optimality cannot be guaranteed in general (abstract).
key_idea: The method handles three named issues: balancing effort between global exploration of the design space and local refinement, keeping the surrogate well conditioned as points pile up locally, and providing a provably convergent mechanism that ensures local optimality (abstract).

method_links.method: Method 1
method_links.note: Global surrogates drive exploration while a provably convergent mechanism ensures local optimality. The abstract does not name the Search/Poll split.

transferable: Plan for surrogate ill-conditioning when sample points cluster near the incumbent. Name it as a design issue with its own mechanism, next to the exploration/refinement balance and the local-convergence safeguard (abstract).
coauthors: J. Dennis (works.json: "J Denni"; presumably J.E. Dennis Jr.), D. Moore, A. Booker, P. Frank

quotes.text: In general, guarantees of global optimality are not possible.
However, a robust surrogate-model-based optimization method is presented here that has good global search properties, and proven local convergence results.

title: New branch-and-cut algorithm for bilevel linear programming

experiments: Randomly generated BLPs; baseline pure branch-and-bound (abstract).
